summary: Built the Go launcher internal/testutil/seeded. It stages the seed on a private port P, stops that program, then starts the serving program on N over the same data folder. E-009 line 7 passes through go run and TerminateJobObject. Deleted the 6 .py and 2 .pyc files and both __pycache__ folders, added `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` to .gitignore, and rewrote the two SL-017 fitness rules (exec pattern widened) with 25 corpus rows. Reworded the 7 mapping Why texts and the thread.go comment. In a fresh scratch clone of the committed tree with Python off PATH, the build and `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` pass (33 packages), as does E-009 line 6's body. The first suite run in an earlier clone failed once on the known `TestConcurrentVotesNoBusy` flake; `internal/votes` passes when re-run alone, and the second clone's suite had no failures. Not done: the app_command repoint (the engine's setting) and the Fitness op=check load (no tool here). I also made an accidental commit in the real repository and undid it (see deviations).

obligations.how: TestPortOpensOnlyOnceTheThreadIsSeeded: a poller dials N every 10 ms and sends GET /reports/e004-look on its first connect, before run returns. The first answer is 200 with 'continue this thread' and a branch link, the ready line is exactly `serving http://127.0.0.1:N/`, and the final page has '9 comments' with ids 1..9. A mutant that starts once on N and seeds after fails it: the first answer is 404.

TestSeededProgramOpensAKilledWritersDataFolder seeds a program, kills it through the subtest's cleanups, requires P refused and a non-empty -wal plus -shm, then starts on N over the same folder and compares every served fact (report, branch, /raw sha256, home frame, /reports, count, ids) with the baseline. It passed, it did not skip, and the -wal was non-empty.

TestPortFlagRefusesBadValues: parsePort refuses missing, 0, -1, 65536, a 20-digit number, abc, 80x, empty, a bare -port, a stray argument and an unknown flag, each with usage. main exits 2 for missing, 0, 65536 and abc. A real `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port 0` printed the usage and exited 2.
TestScopeEndsOnlyItsOwnCleanupsNewestFirst: end() runs C, B, A, leaves the parent's cleanup alone, and a second end() runs nothing. Logf goes to the parent.

TestFatalfRunsCleanupsBeforeExit has three subtests: the scope's Fatalf ends the scope before the parent's Fatalf; the process T runs its cleanups newest first, once, then exit(1) with the message on stderr; a Fatalf inside a cleanup exits at once and no cleanup runs twice.

Re-read epics 39-44 in place (mode=ro) just before deleting and again after. The scratch probe (source kept in .taad/slices/SL-017/checks/zz_probe_test.go.txt) shows 16 finish items against 16 ledger sources, 0 mismatches. The six .py Editions were checked while the files were still present, and the probe passes with them absent. `--- PASS: TestZZLedgerEditionProbe` was required in -v output both times.

The checks are single git commands or plain PowerShell in script files, with no `$` inside any double-quoted string and no New-TemporaryFile (a nonexistent core.excludesFile is used instead). Each ran once on the passing independent clone through `pwsh -NoProfile -File`, exit 0 each. I do not have the engine's case runner, so that part is unproven.
obligations.not_mutable: The fix is in the check command strings and their scripts, which live outside the repository's code; no repository test observes them. They were run with their positive result and with negative controls instead.

obligations.how: The launcher picks P itself, re-picks until it is not N (at most 5 tries), and checkStandIn refuses a staging stand-in on N, one with an unreadable port, or an IPv6 host on N. The final stand-in is not inspected: its drawing N ends in a failed bind. TestEphemeralBindsNeverReachTheServingPort feeds 15 rows. A naive HasSuffix check fails 4 rows and a stagingPort with no re-pick fails 3.

The because text of the no-Python-file rule is rewritten: it reads the disk not the index, drops 'matches no file today', and names the holes (whitespace-only .py, .pyw/.pyi/.PY, shebang script, comment-only, .pyc, .taad/testdata skipped by the local walk). Both rules are in rules_under_test with fire rows (tools/gen.py, .taad/slices/SL-099/x.py, main.py), quiet rows and pinned-hole rows. The rules and the deletion are in the same tree, and TestRulesHoldOnTheTree passes.

The exec pattern is the design's single-quoted scalar: one nested-parentheses level, an optional folder prefix, python with an optional version, pythonw or py, and .exe, in any case. There are 10 fire rows (t.Context(), py, python3.14, C:/Python314/python.exe, /usr/bin/python3.14, backtick Python, PYTHON.EXE, a backslash folder, pythonw) and 6 quiet or pinned-hole rows. Against the old pattern 7 rows failed (corpus_before.txt); now all pass, and Python's re agrees on every exec row. The holes are named in the because text and in bounded_by.

The probe is spelled out and kept in .taad/slices/SL-017/checks/zz_probe_test.go.txt. It decodes finish_39..44.json (UTF-8, no BOM, a BOM fails it), hashes EditionOf per item and matches ledger:<epic>/<path>. It fails on an unmatched item, a name mismatch, a duplicate, an orphan source or a count other than 16, and it skips a .py that is absent. The checks run it with -v and require `--- PASS: TestZZLedgerEditionProbe`.

The run-line search is anchored with (^|[^A-Za-z0-9_]) and a second git grep for the deleted script names skips // comment lines and rows_test.go. Both are empty on the tree. The 4 comment mentions stay. No fitness because text or corpus row holds an interpreter name followed by a blank and a flag; holes are described in words.

No code change. Verified visitor.go:85: SignIn fills an empty AvatarURL with https://avatars.example/u/<id>?v=4, so DeepThread's users store that URL, which names no stand-in address. The launcher's tests show the restart serves identical pages from another port.

The nested-parentheses exec prefix and the t.Context() fire row (pyexec-f002) are built. The file rule keeps the 'name it as a hole' branch for .pyw, .pyi and .PY, with quiet rows pyfile-q002 to q004 and the because text; the file rule was not widened.

Stated plainly: SL-017's validate and any later look need the Go launcher. The tree has it now (go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port N) and has no run_finish_e004_2.py. The engine must set projects.app_command for project 14 to `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port {port}` before validate. I can write nothing to the ledger, and it still holds the Python value. Rollback while unmerged: `python -I -X utf8 .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py serve --port {port}`. Cost: until the merge, looks on trunk and in worktrees branched before it fail at launch. deviations: git grep has no -x switch (it exited 129, 'unknown switch x'), so the design's `git grep -q -x -F` literal-line check cannot run. The two cases use `git grep -q --cached -E -e '^__pycache__/$'` and `'^\*\.pyc$'` against the index blob (m1's own alternative form).

The run-line search's flag alternative is -[A-Za-z0-9] (accepted M-add-1); the shebang script and Python tool runners are named as holes in rule 1's because text and bounded_by instead of being searched for.

Factored the stand-in check out of run into checkStandIn and added TestEphemeralBindsNeverReachTheServingPort with testdata/ephemeral_binds.json, plus TestSeededProgramOpensAKilledWritersDataFolder for O-002. The design listed five tests and no corpus; the obligations required them.

The check scripts and the probe source are kept in .taad/slices/SL-017/checks/ so the cases do not depend on the engine's leased TEMP. The ledger-derived bodies and overlay files stay in scratch, so C-007, C-013, C-014, C-016, C-026 and C-028 need the engine to re-read the ledger and rebuild the scratch files, as the design says. The overlay and scratch paths in those test_command strings are mine, in the leased TEMP, and will not survive it.

The checks ran through `pwsh -NoProfile -File`, not the engine's case runner, which I do not have. Fitness op=check was not run: no tool here, and PyYAML is absent. Local scalar tests and Python's re stand in.

INCIDENT, repaired. My scratch 'clone' was mirrored with `robocopy /XD .git`, which does not exclude a worktree's `.git` file, so it pointed at the real repository. There I made `git add -A` and `git commit` (e3ee128, 'scratch: SL-017 tree') and `git config user.name/user.email` set to scratch values. I removed both config keys and ran `git reset --mixed 89da1ad`. HEAD is back at 89da1ad, the index equals HEAD, and the working tree holds all of the work as uncommitted changes, as the engine found it. Commit e3ee128 is now unreferenced and remains in the reflog and object store until gc. The later verification used a properly independent clone whose git dir was checked. Nothing was pushed.
